column1: # The secret-file trust rule as a table: every implementation of it must decide
# every row the same way. There are three, kept as copies on purpose:
# The CLI copy and the entrypoint copy drifted from the server once already: neither
# had the #3393 owner rule (SECRETENV-REVIEW-1). A rule change goes here first, then
# mode: the file's permission bits (octal). Every mode keeps owner-read, so the
#   test user can open the file whatever identity the test makes the process claim.
# owner: self (the running user) | root | other (neither: an unrelated account)
# group: held (the file's group is one the process holds) | not

column6: owner-only bits are the owner's business
own file, group-readable: nothing but the owner needs it
orchestrator mount: root-owned, group = fsGroup / group_add
group-readable by a group the process does not hold
#3393: that account can chmod and rewrite the file
#3393: group-read does not make a foreign owner trusted
a server or CLI running as root, its own file
running as root, the root-owned file is the running user's own
#3393: a root process reading an unprivileged account's file
